screen4-a1.glyph: two horizontal lines, the lower one shorter
screen4-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Menu" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen4-a1.convention_relied_on: two/three stacked lines = open the main menu (hamburger) - my reading; the two-line variant is slightly less canonical than three lines
screen4-a1.initial_rationale: no label, but two stacked horizontal lines is a recognizable variant of the hamburger menu convention - common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test
screen4-a1.deciding_evidence: tapping it slid a navigation drawer in from the left, exactly what the menu convention promises; the missing label is not a barrier; tested once on screen1-a1 and carried to this identical control

screen4-a2.description: pill in the header with a sparkle glyph and the words 'Get Plus'
screen4-a2.location: pill in the header with a sparkle glyph and the words 'Get Plus'
screen4-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Get Plus" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen4-a2.initial_rationale: visible words 'Get Plus' with a sparkle; 'Plus' is a product name a first-time user has no way to decode, and nothing says it costs money
screen4-a2.deciding_evidence: tapping opened a paywall ('ChatGPT Plus', 'Upgrade for $19.99', 'Renews monthly') - a paid monthly subscription the words 'Get Plus' never mentioned; tested once on screen1-a2 and carried to this identical control
screen4-a2.recommendation: say what it is and that it is paid, e.g. 'Upgrade to Plus (paid plan)'

screen4-a3.glyph: speech bubble drawn with a broken outline
screen4-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Temporary chat" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen4-a3.initial_rationale: a speech bubble drawn with a broken outline is not an established convention and carries no label
screen4-a3.deciding_evidence: no tooltip on long-press and no visible text in any state before activation; the words 'Temporary chat' appear only on the screen the tap opens; tested once on screen1-a3 and carried to this identical control
screen4-a3.recommendation: add a visible label beside or under the glyph, e.g. 'Temporary chat (not saved)'

screen4-a9.accessibility_text_consulted: no strings on the record; not used in the verdict
screen4-a9.initial_rationale: placeholder 'Write anything' says nothing about what the box is for in this context - the text to be edited, or an instruction about it

test_cases.precondition: 'Write or edit' panel open, composer empty
test_cases.expected_result: the field reveals what kind of input it wants
test_cases.confirms_if: it accepts anything and never says whether it wants text-to-edit or an instruction
test_cases.overturns_if: a hint or label says what to paste or type
test_cases.observed_result: 'Hello' was accepted, the placeholder vanished, send turned blue; no hint said what the box expected

screen4-a9.deciding_evidence: the box accepted 'Hello' exactly as it would a request, and nothing on screen said whether to paste the writing to edit or to describe what is wanted
screen4-a9.recommendation: replace the placeholder with a specific instruction, e.g. 'Paste the text you want help with'

screen4-a10.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Dictation" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen4-a10.convention_relied_on: microphone = speak instead of typing - my reading
screen4-a10.initial_rationale: unlabeled microphone; microphone = speak / voice input is an established convention - exemption pending test
screen4-a10.deciding_evidence: tapping raised the system request to record audio - the microphone convention held (permission was denied per safety rules); tested once on screen1-a9 and carried to this identical control

screen4-a11.glyph: blue filled circle with vertical sound-wave bars
screen4-a11.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Start a voice conversation" - read only to know what to watch for when testing; not used in the verdict
screen4-a11.initial_rationale: a filled circle with vertical sound-wave bars is not an established convention a first-time user would read, and it carries no label
screen4-a11.deciding_evidence: no label in any state before the tap; only after tapping does a dialog mention 'Voice', and the control sits right beside a microphone, so the two voice controls are not told apart; tested once on screen1-a10 and carried to this identical control
screen4-a11.recommendation: label it, e.g. 'Talk with ChatGPT' beside the glyph, and distinguish it from the dictation microphone
